proposals.impact: convert the one session that bounced at intro_load into a quiz start
proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours the quiz had one session and zero starts. The furthest step reached was intro_load, meaning someone landed on the quiz intro page and left before pressing anything. With a content queue at 1 and no new email signups tracked, the quiz is the primary active acquisition point right now. A single friction point at the intro screen is costing every visitor Joel is sending there.
proposals.proposal: The intro screen is doing too much explaining before it asks for anything. The current text likely describes the quiz at length, which gives a hesitant visitor reasons to think rather than reasons to begin. Replace the intro copy with something that names the specific discomfort the ICP already feels, states exactly what will happen (four questions, two minutes), and puts the button in the first eyeline. No spiritual framing, no promise of transformation. Just a plain description of what the quiz surfaces and why that is worth two minutes of a Monday morning.
proposals.current_text: Take our free money psychology quiz to discover your money personality type and get personalised insights to transform your relationship with money.
proposals.new_text: Most people who earn well and still feel behind are not bad with money. They are responding to a pattern that formed long before they had any. This quiz takes two minutes and four questions. It identifies which of three money behaviour patterns is most likely running the gap between what you earn and what you actually keep. No email required to see your result.

proposals.impact: lift Money Worship open rate from 37.5% toward the 66.67% Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: Money Vigilance has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends. Money Worship sits at 37.5% across 16 sends. That is a 29-percentage-point gap, which at this list size is not noise. The sequences are presumably delivering to people who selected those profiles from the same quiz, so the audience intent is comparable. The difference is most likely in subject line specificity. Vigilance subscribers are probably more anxious and therefore more responsive to precise, low-stakes subject lines. Worship subscribers may be receiving subject lines that feel either too celebratory or too generic.
proposals.proposal: Pull the subject line from email-01 in the Money Worship sequence and rewrite it to match the register that is working in Vigilance. The Worship pattern in behavioural economics describes people who equate money with self-worth and status, so the subject line should name a specific, slightly uncomfortable truth about that pattern rather than something that sounds like a reward. The goal is to make the Worship subscriber feel seen in a way that earns the open, not celebrated in a way that lets them scroll past.
proposals.current_text: Subject: Your money personality result: Money Worship
proposals.new_text: Subject: You're good at earning it. Here's why keeping it feels different.

proposals.impact: restore automated content publishing — queue is at 1 and three workflows failed overnight
proposals.observation: Three workflows failed overnight: Daily Blog Post at 06:34, Weekly Monday Report at 08:50, and Funnel-Hack Digest at 12:01. The content queue is at 1 post queued and 47 published. The Daily Blog Post failure means no new post went out today, which compounds across the week if the root cause is not fixed. The two commits in the last 24 hours touched Slack alerting for lead-magnet captures and a quiz cursor update, neither of which would explain these failures directly. The most likely cause is a shared dependency: an API key rotation, a rate limit, or a schema change that all three workflows hit in sequence.
proposals.proposal: Open the daily-blog-post.yml workflow log for the 06:34 run and read the step that failed. The exit code and error message will tell Joel whether this is an environment secret issue (likely if all three failed in sequence with similar errors), a content schema validation error (likely if a recent Astro config change broke frontmatter parsing), or an external API timeout. Once the failure step is identified, fix the environment variable name or add a null-check on the API response in the workflow's run step. Do not touch astro.config.mjs or .github/workflows directly per the safety rules — flag the specific line to a developer with the error output attached.
proposals.new_text:
